architect.title: Architect
architect.desc: Designs buildings and the documents that get them built. Balances program, code, budget, and intent across years-long projects.

license.label: State architecture license (RA/ARB) — registration required to practice/title

computational-designer.title: Computational Designer
computational-designer.desc: Turns design intent into code. Writes algorithms and scripts to generate geometry, automate documentation, and solve problems that would be impossible by hand.

bim-manager.title: BIM Manager
bim-manager.desc: Owns the digital model across a project team. Sets standards, coordinates disciplines, and makes sure every drawing in the set comes from one source of truth.

creative-technologist.title: Creative Technologist
creative-technologist.desc: Sits between design and engineering. Builds prototypes and interactive experiences for brands, museums, and studios — making technical ideas physical and legible.

data-analyst.title: Data Analyst
data-analyst.desc: Turns messy business data into decisions. Runs the queries, builds the dashboards, and translates what patterns actually mean for the people making the calls.

ux-designer.title: UX Designer
ux-designer.desc: Designs how software should feel to use. Researches users, maps flows, sketches interfaces, and defends the human experience against every other project pressure.

product-designer.title: Product Designer
product-designer.desc: Owns a digital product's look, feel, and story end to end. Combines visual design, systems thinking, and close collaboration with engineers and PMs.

urban-planner.title: Urban Planner
urban-planner.desc: Shapes cities and neighborhoods over years, not weeks. Works with public policy, GIS data, and community input to design zoning, mobility, and public space.

license.label: Brokerage/contractor licenses depending on activity
Often requires PE/RA background
PE license required to sign/seal structural work
PE license required for sign-off roles
CPA license required for public accounting/attest work
FINRA licenses required for securities roles; CFA common
CPA typically required for external audit
Credentialing exams (SOA/CAS) effectively required
State insurance licenses for some lines
Licenses/certifications by sector (FINRA, AML)
Bar admission required — jurisdiction-specific
State RN license (NCLEX) required
State APRN license + national certification required
Certification (CMA/RMA) commonly expected; varies by state
DPT degree + state PT license (NPTE) required
PharmD + state pharmacist license (NAPLEX) required
RD/RDN credential + state licensure in most states
Certifications (ACRP/SoCRA) commonly expected
State clinical license (LPC/LMFT/LCSW) required
State license required for clinical roles (LCSW)
State psychologist license required
State teaching certification required for public schools
State administrator certification typically required
PE required for sign-off roles; not for most product/manufacturing roles
PE required for public-facing/utility sign-off; not for product roles
State license + EPA 608 certification required
Food-safety certification (ServSafe) typically required

architectural-drafter.title: Architectural Drafter
architectural-drafter.desc: Turns an architect's design into the precise drawings a project gets built from. Lives in Revit and AutoCAD; owns the accuracy of the set.

teaching-assistant.title: Teaching Assistant
teaching-assistant.desc: Supports a classroom teacher and the students who need the most help. The most common way into the education profession.

license.label: Paraprofessional requirements vary by state

maintenance-technician.title: Maintenance Technician
maintenance-technician.desc: Keeps equipment and buildings running. Diagnoses faults, makes repairs, and prevents the breakdowns before they happen.

police-officer.title: Police Officer
police-officer.desc: Enforces the law and responds to incidents in a community. Public-sector work with clear rank structure and pension.

license.label: Police academy + state certification (POST) required

ai-engineer.title: AI Engineer
ai-engineer.desc: Builds products on top of large language models and machine-learning systems — retrieval pipelines, agents, evaluation, and the engineering that makes AI reliable in production.

mlops-engineer.title: MLOps Engineer
mlops-engineer.desc: Owns the path from model to production: training pipelines, deployment, monitoring, drift, and the infrastructure that keeps machine learning running.

prompt-engineer.title: Prompt Engineer
prompt-engineer.desc: Designs, tests, and versions the instructions that steer large language models — prompt systems, evaluation suites, and guardrails for AI products.

computer-vision-engineer.title: Computer Vision Engineer
computer-vision-engineer.desc: Teaches machines to see: detection, segmentation, tracking, and imaging pipelines for products from robotics to medical imaging.

nlp-engineer.title: NLP Engineer
nlp-engineer.desc: Builds systems that read and write language — classification, extraction, search, and LLM-based applications over text.

robotics-engineer.title: Robotics Engineer
robotics-engineer.desc: Designs and programs robots — kinematics, control systems, perception, and the integration of hardware with autonomy software.

ai-product-manager.title: AI Product Manager
ai-product-manager.desc: Product management where the product is a model: scoping AI capabilities, evaluation criteria, data strategy, and shipping ML-powered features responsibly.

data-architect.title: Data Architect
data-architect.desc: Designs how an organization's data lives: warehouses, lakes, models, governance, and the pipelines between them.

cook.title: Cook
cook.desc: Prepares and plates food to order on a working line, under time and consistency pressure. Distinct from the chef who runs the kitchen.

automotive-technician.title: Automotive Technician
automotive-technician.desc: Diagnoses and repairs vehicles, from brakes and diagnostics to full engine work. Includes auto, diesel, and heavy-equipment technicians.

physician.title: Physician
physician.desc: Diagnoses and treats illness across a specialty, from primary care to surgery. Long training and licensure gate the role.

license.label: MD/DO, residency, and state medical license (7+ yrs of training)

paramedic.title: Paramedic
paramedic.desc: Delivers emergency medical care in the field and in transit, from ambulances to air rescue. Licensed, high-stakes, and shift-based. EMT is the tier below, not a synonym.

license.label: State paramedic license (NREMT); 1–2 yr accredited program

dental-hygienist.title: Dental Hygienist
dental-hygienist.desc: Cleans teeth, takes radiographs, and screens for oral disease alongside a dentist. A licensed clinical profession, one tier above dental assisting.

license.label: State RDH license; accredited dental-hygiene associate degree (~3 yrs)

medical-scribe.title: Medical Scribe
medical-scribe.desc: Documents a clinician's visits in real time so the clinician can focus on the patient. A common on-ramp into healthcare and medical school.

developer-advocate.title: Developer Advocate
developer-advocate.desc: The bridge between a technical product and the developers who use it: docs, demos, talks, and feedback carried back to engineering.

penetration-tester.title: Penetration Tester
penetration-tester.desc: Attacks systems on purpose, with permission, to find the holes before an adversary does. Offensive security, red-teaming, and reporting.

growth-marketer.title: Growth Marketer
growth-marketer.desc: Owns a growth number and runs experiments across acquisition, activation, and retention. Half marketer, half analyst.

conversation-designer.title: Conversation Designer
conversation-designer.desc: Designs how people talk to software: chatbots, voice assistants, and the scripts and flows behind conversational AI.

data-annotator.title: Data Annotator
data-annotator.desc: Labels and rates the data that trains and aligns machine-learning models, including the human feedback behind modern AI.

genetic-counselor.title: Genetic Counselor
genetic-counselor.desc: Interprets genetic test results and guides patients through the risks and decisions that follow. Master's-level and licensed.

license.label: Master's in genetic counseling + ABGC board certification; state licensure in most states

forensic-accountant.title: Forensic Accountant
forensic-accountant.desc: Follows the money through fraud, disputes, and investigations. Accounting used as evidence rather than record-keeping.

cartographer.title: Cartographer
cartographer.desc: Turns spatial data into maps and models, from survey to screen. Overlaps GIS but centered on the map itself.

drone-pilot.title: Drone Pilot
drone-pilot.desc: Flies uncrewed aircraft for survey, inspection, film, and delivery. Commercial work requires a remote-pilot certificate.

perfusionist.title: Perfusionist
perfusionist.desc: Runs the heart-lung machine that keeps a patient alive during cardiac surgery. A small field with high stakes and specialized training.

patent-agent.title: Patent Agent
patent-agent.desc: Drafts and prosecutes patents before the patent office. Technical enough to read the invention, credentialed without being a lawyer.

robotics-technician.title: Robotics Technician
robotics-technician.desc: Builds, calibrates, and maintains robots and automated lines on the floor. The hands-on complement to the robotics engineer.

medical-sales-representative.title: Medical Sales Representative
medical-sales-representative.desc: Sells prescription drugs, devices or diagnostics to clinicians and hospitals on an assigned territory.

quality-inspector.title: Quality Inspector
quality-inspector.desc: Checks parts, products, vehicles or cargo against a specification and signs off or rejects them.

laboratory-technician.title: Laboratory Technician
laboratory-technician.desc: Runs samples, instruments and tests in a laboratory and records the results.

machinist.title: Machinist
machinist.desc: Sets up and runs lathes, mills and CNC machines to cut metal parts to a drawing.

construction-superintendent.title: Construction Superintendent
construction-superintendent.desc: Runs the site day to day: crews, subcontractors, sequence, safety and the schedule.

project-scheduler.title: Project Scheduler
project-scheduler.desc: Builds and maintains the programme for a project: activities, logic, resources and the critical path.

quantity-surveyor.title: Quantity Surveyor
quantity-surveyor.desc: Prices, measures and controls the cost of construction work from tender to final account.

engineering-manager.title: Engineering Manager
engineering-manager.desc: Leads a team of engineers: hiring, priorities, delivery and the people work.

program-manager.title: Program Manager
program-manager.desc: Coordinates a set of related projects toward one outcome, across teams and over years.

systems-engineer.title: Systems Engineer
systems-engineer.desc: Owns how the parts of a complex product fit together: requirements, interfaces, integration and verification.

manufacturing-engineer.title: Manufacturing Engineer
manufacturing-engineer.desc: Designs how a product gets made: the process, the tooling, the line and its yield.

test-engineer.title: Test Engineer
test-engineer.desc: Plans and runs the tests that prove hardware does what its design says, and writes up what it did instead.

electronics-technician.title: Electronics Technician
electronics-technician.desc: Builds, tests and repairs electronic assemblies and instrumentation.

hardware-engineer.title: Hardware Engineer
hardware-engineer.desc: Designs boards, chips and RF front ends: schematics, layout, bring-up.

health-safety-officer.title: Health and Safety Officer
health-safety-officer.desc: Keeps people from getting hurt at work: risk assessments, inspections, incident investigation, compliance.

security-guard.title: Security Guard
security-guard.desc: Protects people, premises and goods on site: patrols, access control, screening, response.

procurement-specialist.title: Procurement Specialist
procurement-specialist.desc: Buys what the company needs: suppliers, tenders, contracts, prices and lead times.

logistics-coordinator.title: Logistics Coordinator
logistics-coordinator.desc: Moves goods on time: carriers, customs, shipping paperwork, dangerous goods, the warehouse handoff.

chemist.title: Chemist
chemist.desc: Analyses, formulates and characterises substances in a lab, and writes the method down.

dental-assistant.title: Dental Assistant
dental-assistant.desc: Works chairside with the dentist: instruments, suction, x-rays, sterilisation, the patient.

dentist.title: Dentist
dentist.desc: Diagnoses and treats teeth, gums and mouths, in general practice or a specialty.

license.label: Dental degree (DDS/DMD or equivalent) and a state or cantonal licence to practise

veterinarian.title: Veterinarian
veterinarian.desc: Diagnoses and treats animals, from companion pets to herds, and advises the people who keep them.

license.label: Veterinary degree (DVM or equivalent) and a state or cantonal licence to practise

occupational-therapist.title: Occupational Therapist
occupational-therapist.desc: Helps people do the everyday things an illness, injury or disability got in the way of.

license.label: Occupational therapy degree and state licence (NBCOT in the US)

emt.title: EMT
emt.desc: Responds to emergencies and gives basic life support on the way to hospital.

license.label: EMT certification (NREMT or state) at the basic or advanced level

pharmacy-technician.title: Pharmacy Technician
pharmacy-technician.desc: Prepares and dispenses medicines under a pharmacist, and keeps the stock and the records straight.

food-service-worker.title: Food Service Worker
food-service-worker.desc: Keeps a kitchen or counter running: prep, plating, dishes, stock, the pace of service.

waiter.title: Waiter
waiter.desc: Takes the order, brings the food and drink, and reads the table.

receptionist.title: Receptionist
receptionist.desc: First face and voice of the place: welcomes, checks in, answers, routes, keeps the desk running.

administrative-assistant.title: Administrative Assistant
administrative-assistant.desc: Keeps an office or a team organised: calendars, documents, orders, the phone, the follow-ups.

project-engineer.title: Project Engineer
project-engineer.desc: The engineer on a project who turns the design into a delivered thing: scope, submittals, vendors, the site.

general-manager.title: General Manager
general-manager.desc: Runs a site, branch, region or business unit end to end, with the P&L.

production-supervisor.title: Production Supervisor
production-supervisor.desc: Runs a shift or a line: people, output, quality, safety, the plan for tomorrow.

payroll-specialist.title: Payroll Specialist
payroll-specialist.desc: Gets everyone paid correctly and on time, and keeps the tax and social filings right.

erp-consultant.title: ERP Consultant
erp-consultant.desc: Configures and rolls out enterprise systems (SAP, Dynamics, Workday, Salesforce) for the people who have to use them.

manufacturing-technician.title: Manufacturing Technician
manufacturing-technician.desc: Builds the product on the floor: assembly, machines, process steps, the paperwork that proves it.

content-moderator.title: Content Moderator
content-moderator.desc: Reviews what people post against the rules of the platform, and decides.

business-development-manager.title: Business Development Manager
business-development-manager.desc: Finds and opens the next accounts, partners and markets, before there is a pipeline to manage.

housekeeper.title: Housekeeper
housekeeper.desc: Keeps rooms, wards, offices and buildings clean and ready, to a standard and a clock.
